summary: Present 1964 R-6 flattop cab on a 10-foot concrete base, after a CCC-era cab; now an $80/night overnight rental in mid-July to mid-September.

facts.design: R-6 flattop cab, 15 by 15 feet, with catwalk, on a 10-foot concrete block base (present tower, 1964); the earlier 1930s cab was an L-4

access.note: Overnight rental, $80 a night, four-person maximum; open mid-July to mid-September. Gravel access; 4WD may be needed per the Forest Service.

visit.trail_note: Gravel road: about 6 miles of Brush Creek Road, then 6.5 miles on Forest Road 215 to the summit (Carbon County guide).

corrections.why: The NHLR, the Forest Service and the Carbon County guide all date the present R-6 tower to 1964. No source read gives 1969.

corrections.proposed: R-6 flattop cab, 15 by 15 feet, on a 10-foot concrete block base (present tower, 1964); L-4 was the earlier 1930s cab
corrections.why: The L-4 was the earlier 1930s cab, replaced by the present R-6 flattop.
Sources give a 10-foot concrete block base, not a total tower height; the 3.0 m in the record matches the base.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The NHLR and the Carbon County guide give 10,788 ft (3,288 m), matching the brief's 3288.2 m; firelookout.com gives 10,816 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
The NHLR says Saratoga Ranger District; the Forest Service page says Brush Creek Ranger District. The story names only the forest.
The Forest Service says a 4WD may be needed; the Carbon County guide says a high-clearance vehicle is recommended and 4WD is not needed. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 1969 build date is contradicted by three sources (1964); Wilma Perue's 1969-1971 tenure may be the source of the mix-up. Rental fee comes from a Forest Service page last updated June 6, 2025; confirm before publishing. The record's kind 'two_story' is not supported by any source read: the NHLR describes a single R-6 cab with an interpretive site on a lower level. No fire or move history found; the CCC-era cab is undated beyond the 1930s.
